what_it_is.prose: Lockheed Martin Aeronautics is the combat-aircraft and airlifter business of US prime Lockheed Martin Corporation. Its Indian military-aerospace footprint has three strands. First, the Indian Air Force operates 12 C-130J-30 Super Hercules tactical airlifters (inducted from 2011), supported under Lockheed Martin sustainment contracts. Second, Lockheed's Hyderabad joint venture with Tata Advanced Systems — Tata Lockheed Martin Aerostructures Limited (TLMAL, established 2010, Atlas slug tlmal) — is the global single source of empennage (tail) assemblies for the C-130J and LM-100J, having delivered its 200th empennage by August 2023 and more than 220 by September 2024; it also builds the C-130J centre wing box and, since a March 2023 agreement, F-16 fighter wings for Lockheed's global supply chain, with the first Made-in-India F-16 wing (a 9G, 12,000-hour interchangeable wing, >70% Indian parts) certified on 7 December 2021. Third, Lockheed has offered the F-21 (an F-16 derivative) for the IAF's Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft (MRFA) requirement, using TLMAL's wing capability as the industrial basis, and on 10 September 2024 signed a teaming agreement with TASL to pursue an in-country C-130J MRO facility for the IAF fleet and future Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) assembly in India. Lockheed retains platform design authority and type certification in the USA; India's role is aerostructure manufacture and assembly. This dossier focuses on the military-aerospace footprint and does not infer an indigenous-content percentage for US-controlled platform IP, avionics and engines.

deployments_procurement.summary: Lockheed's India footprint combines an in-service IAF C-130J-30 fleet (12 aircraft), the TLMAL aerostructures JV in Hyderabad (global sole-source C-130J empennage; Made-in-India F-16 wings), a September 2024 TASL teaming agreement for in-country C-130J MRO and MTA, and an F-21 fighter offer for the MRFA requirement.

faq.question: What is Lockheed Martin's footprint in Indian military aerospace?
faq.answer: Three strands: the Indian Air Force operates 12 C-130J-30 Super Hercules airlifters; Lockheed's Hyderabad JV with Tata (TLMAL) is the global sole source of C-130J empennages and builds Made-in-India F-16 wings; and Lockheed offers the F-21 (an F-16 derivative) for the IAF's MRFA fighter requirement. A September 2024 teaming agreement with Tata Advanced Systems targets in-country C-130J MRO and future Medium Transport Aircraft assembly.

faq.question: What does the TLMAL joint venture make?
faq.answer: Tata Lockheed Martin Aerostructures Limited (TLMAL), a Tata Advanced Systems-Lockheed Martin JV at Adibatla near Hyderabad (est. 2010), is the global single source of empennage (tail) assemblies for the C-130J Super Hercules and LM-100J — over 220 delivered by September 2024. It also builds the C-130J centre wing box and, since 2023, F-16 fighter wings; the first Made-in-India F-16 wing (>70% Indian parts) was certified on 7 December 2021.

faq.question: Is Lockheed's F-21 in Indian service?
faq.answer: No. The F-21 is an F-16-derived fighter Lockheed Martin has offered for the IAF's Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft (MRFA) requirement, with TLMAL's Hyderabad wing capability cited as the industrial basis. It has not been selected. Lockheed's in-service Indian platform is the C-130J-30 (12 aircraft).
